thread:
marta: heads up — noticed a regression after last night's kms rewrap. API keys that were scoped to "embeddings:generate" are being allowed to call /v1/chat/completions via our routing fallback.

devin: whoa. any logs?

marta: pasted excerpt from prod auth log: 
```
auth.check: api_key_id=ak_12345 action=ALLOW reason=route-fallback granted_scopes=[] requested_route=/v1/chat/completions requested_model=text-chat-3
```
I also see the key metadata in kms shows tag `scope=embeddings:generate`, but the auth service appears to have an empty granted_scopes array.

samir: could be the auth cache TTL or the scope-cache strip during rewrap. last rewrap job touched the metadata migration script.

karen: is the policy enforcement happening in the runtime proxy or in the auth service?

marta: enforcement should be in auth service (pre-routing), but our runtime has an extra fallback policy: if auth denies a route but allows model access it will try model-level evaluation. looks like model-level check is passing and fallback is flipping ALLOW.

devin: reproduce steps?

marta: 1) call embeddings endpoint with header `Authorization: Bearer ak_12345` 2) call chat endpoint with same key 3) observe chat call succeeds.

samir: quick dump from service shows the auth cache entry post-rotate: `api_key_id=ak_12345 scopes=[] metadata_tags={kms_tag: rewrap_2026}` — tags are present but scopes array empty. suspect kube-proxy sidecar stripped X-Api-Scopes header on internal call.

karen: can we confirm whether DB still has the scope? If KMS rewrap only touched crypto we shouldn't lose DB metadata.

marta: DB check: `select scopes from api_keys where id='ak_12345'` returns `{"embeddings:generate"}` — so DB ok.

devin: then path is: request -> proxy -> auth-service -> cache write. somewhere between proxy and auth the scope meta is lost. any recent changes to auth client?

marta: yes, the rotate job introduced a tiny helper that rehydrates metadata from KMS and POSTs to /internal/auth/refresh with JSON payload. that helper serializes using content-type `text/plain` by mistake in one patch. auth-service falling back and ignoring body when content-type mismatch. so granted_scopes becomes empty array.

samir: lol. content-type bugs are the best.

karen: plan? mitigation first: update runtime to block route-fallback so that an empty granted_scopes results in DENY, not fallback allow. we should also hotfix the rotate helper to send proper `application/json` and re-run refresh for affected keys.

marta: agreed. propose steps: 
- @devin please push a runtime config change to opt-out route-fallback for auth failures (can be a flag) — small rollout to prod by region.
- @samir patch rotate helper to set correct content-type and add retry, then re-run migration for keys touched last night.
- @karen add an audit log assertion: any auth grant must include `granted_scopes` non-empty or else emit `auth:missing_scopes` event.

devin: taking runtime flag, will ship canary in us-west-2 in 30m. :eyes:

samir: patching rotate helper now. also adding a unit test for content-type.

marta: I'll run a script to re-run refresh for keys with kms_tag rewrap_2026 and add a quick query to enumerate keys whose last_refresh < rewrap time.

sec-bot: incident created: SEC-2026-07 — scope-drop-on-rewrap. severity=high. assigned_to=eng-security.

deploy-bot: canary deployed to us-west-2 (devin). health checks passing.

karen: also, add a one-line note in postmortems channel after we close. and add a regression test in auth-integration harness that simulates content-type mismatch.

marta: thanks team. will follow up with a short remediation runbook once we confirm mass re-refresh succeeded. :+1:
